data.name: Lilia
data.gender_notes: Lilia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word leíon, meaning 'lily'. In ancient Greece, the lily was a symbol of purity and innocence. In the Bible, lilies are often used as symbols of the resurrection. The name Lilia carries the meaning “Lily flower” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lilia usually hope their child will grow to embody lily flower and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Lilia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lily flower.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lilia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: ליליה
in_hebrew.meaning: ליליה היא פרח השקד או הלילה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ליליה הוא שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו היא פרח השקד או הלילה. השם ליליה קשור לשקדיה, שהם סמלים של יופי ושל רוך. בהקשר הרוחני, השם ליליה יכול לייצג את היופי והרכות של הנפש.

in_greek.name: Λιλία
in_greek.meaning: Λιλία σημαίνει κρίνος ή λευκός κρίνος
in_greek.long_meaning: Λιλία είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει κρίνος ή λευκός κρίνος. Ο κρίνος είναι σύμβολο της αγνότητας και της καθαρότητας. Στην πνευματική του σημασία, το όνομα Λιλία μπορεί να αντιπροσωπεύει την αγνότητα και την πνευματική ομορφιά.

in_latin.name: Lilia
in_latin.long_meaning: Lilia est nomen quod originem habet in lingua Latina et significat lilium seu puritas. Lilium est flos qui puritatem et innocentiam repraesentat. In contextu spirituali, nomen Lilia potest significare puritatem cordis et spiritus.

in_english.name: Lilia
in_english.meaning: Lilia means Lily or pure one
in_english.long_meaning: Lilia is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning Lily or pure one. The lily flower is a symbol of purity, innocence, and refined beauty. In the biblical context, the lily is mentioned in the Song of Solomon as a symbol of love and purity. Historically, the name Lilia has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person's spiritual purity and moral integrity. The name Lilia conveys a sense of elegance, modesty, and spiritual depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lilia has a rich cultural history, being derived from the ancient Greek word leíon, meaning 'lily'. In many cultures throughout history, lilies have been symbols of purity and innocence. In ancient Greece, a lily was often depicted in statues or paintings as a symbol of the goddess Hera, who was known as the queen of the heavens and the goddess of marriage, motherhood, childbirth, and women's fertility.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Lilia has deep significance, as it is derived from the symbolic flower of the lily. In the Bible, lilies are mentioned in several passages, including Matthew 6:28-30, where Jesus teaches that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed as beautifully as a lily. Lilies are also used as symbols of the resurrection, as they are one of the few flowers that bloom in the spring after a long winter, representing new life and the promise of eternal life. Additionally, in many Christian traditions, the lily represents the pure and sinless life of the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lilia represents the purity and innocence of the lily flower, symbolizing the gentle and peaceful soul of a Christian woman. It also signifies the resurrection and the promise of eternal life, as the lily blooms most beautifully after the winter season.

historical_references.reference: In ancient Rome, Lilia was the name of a Vestal Virgin. Vestal Virgins were priestesses devoted to the goddess Vesta, the guardian of the Roman hearth. They were known for their chastity and purity, and were highly revered in Roman society. Lilia is mentioned in several ancient Roman texts, including those by the historian Livy and the poet Ovid.

During the Middle Ages, Lilia was a popular name for Christian saints. Saint Lilia of Siena is one such example, who lived in the 13th century. She was a noblewoman from Siena who renounced her wealthy lifestyle and dedicated herself to a life of poverty and prayer. Her feast day is celebrated on October 11.
